strings.What is the break even point?: What is the break even point?
strings.It is the sales volume at which total re: It is the sales volume at which total revenue equals the fixed and variable costs included in the analysis. At that volume, the modeled total profit is zero.
strings.How do I calculate break even units?: How do I calculate break even units?
strings.Subtract variable cost per unit from sel: Subtract variable cost per unit from selling price per unit, then divide fixed costs by that contribution margin. The formula requires a positive contribution margin to give a usable sales target.
strings.Fixed costs are costs that do not change: Fixed costs are costs that do not change with sales volume within the range and period you are modeling, such as a monthly lease or a fixed software subscription. Classify costs consistently for your own business.
strings.What counts as variable cost per unit?: What counts as variable cost per unit?
strings.Variable costs change with the number of: Variable costs change with the number of units sold. They may include materials, packaging, or per-sale fees. Use the variable cost for one unit, not the total for all units.
strings.Is Profit Per Unit the same as net profi: Is Profit Per Unit the same as net profit?
strings.No. Here it means selling price minus va: No. Here it means selling price minus variable cost per unit, also called contribution margin per unit. That amount helps cover fixed costs before creating total business profit.
strings.What happens if contribution margin is z: What happens if contribution margin is zero?
strings.With positive fixed costs, sales cannot: With positive fixed costs, sales cannot cover those fixed costs because each unit contributes zero. Break even units and revenue display N/A. If fixed costs are also zero, the model is already at break even at zero sales and remains there at any sales volume.
strings.What happens if contribution margin is n: What happens if contribution margin is negative?
strings.Each sale increases the modeled loss. Wi: Each sale increases the modeled loss. With positive fixed costs, there is no nonnegative break even sales volume. If fixed costs are zero, zero sales is the break even point, but any positive sales volume creates a loss.
strings.Should I round break even units up?: Should I round break even units up?
strings.For indivisible products, round the unro: For indivisible products, round the unrounded formula result up to a whole unit. The main result shows the theoretical quantity, while the result note shows a whole-unit target. Break even revenue uses the unrounded theoretical quantity.
strings.What happens when fixed costs are zero?: What happens when fixed costs are zero?
strings.Zero sales covers zero fixed costs, so b: Zero sales covers zero fixed costs, so break even units and revenue are zero. Positive contribution margin makes each additional sale profitable in this model; negative contribution margin makes each additional sale a loss.
strings.Can I use this for several products?: Can I use this for several products?
strings.This calculator models one product or a: This calculator models one product or a representative unit. Products with different prices and variable costs need a weighted contribution margin based on an assumed sales mix. Changing that mix changes the result.

strings.ROAS stands for return on advertising sp: ROAS stands for return on advertising spend. It compares revenue attributed to advertising with the amount spent on those ads.
strings.Divide revenue generated by advertising: Divide revenue generated by advertising spend. Revenue of 4000 with spend of 1000 gives a ROAS ratio of 4, displayed as 4.00x or 4.00:1, and a ROAS percentage of 400%.
strings.There is no universal target. A useful b: There is no universal target. A useful benchmark depends on your contribution margin, costs, attribution method, and business objectives. Compare against your own consistently measured campaigns and the revenue needed to cover all relevant costs.

strings.A 1.00x ROAS means attributed revenue eq: A 1.00x ROAS means attributed revenue equals ad spend. It covers advertising spend only; product costs, fees, shipping, and overhead can still make the business lose money.

strings.ROI stands for return on investment. It: ROI stands for return on investment. It measures a gain or loss relative to the amount invested, expressed as a percentage. This calculator uses simple ROI: it compares a starting investment with a total final return over the period you choose.
strings.Final Return means the total amount rece: Final Return means the total amount received or ending value, including recovered capital. If you invest $10,000 and finish with $12,500, the final return is $12,500 and the profit is $2,500.
